caseno:
Civil Revision No. 305 of 2003
With
Civil Revision No. 974 of 2003
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim with Mr. H.N. Nondy and Mr. Kh. Aminul Haque, Advocates ----- for the petitioner of Cr. No. 305/2003 and opposite party of C.R. No. 974/2003
Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Sultan Mahmud & Ms. Bilkis Jahan, Advocates ----- for the Opposite parties of Civil Rev. No. 305/2003 and petitioner of Civil Revision No. 974/2003
parties:
Md. Shahjahan Miah
Vs.
Md. Mustaque Hossain and another
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Aziz, J:- In Civil Revision No. 305/2003 Rule was issued at the instance of Md. Shahjahan Miah, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the order dated 28.11.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 6/2002 should not be set aside. 

 2. In Civil Revision No. 974 of 2003 Rule was issued at the instance of Md. Mustaque Hossain, upon the opposite party No. 1 Md. Shahjahan Mia to show cause as to why the order dated 4.3.2003 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2002 should not be set aside. 

 5. Opposite party No. 2 Md. Abdul Hye who was defendant No. 1 in the suit contested the suit by filing written statements. The learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka decreed the suit against him on contest and ex parte against opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain who was defendant No. 2 in the suit vide it's judgment dated 17.11.1997. The opposite party no. 2 filed C.R. case No. 377/1998 under section 25 of Small Causes Courts Act before the High Court Division against the aforesaid judgment and decree and a single Bench of the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 3.11.98 sent the case back on remand to the trial court for re-trial making the rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court. The petitioner filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 662/1999 before the Appellate Division against the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division impleading both the defendant opposite parties. The Appeal No. 105/1999 arose which was allowed on contest vide judgment dated 24.10.2000. The opposite party No. 2 made Civil Review Petition bearing No. 64/2001 against the same which was also rejected by the Appellate Division vide its order dated 29.4.02. In the meantime the opposite party No. 1 Md. Mostaque Hossain, who was defendant no. 2 in the suit started Miscellaneous Case No. 85 of 1997 renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 2002 on an application field by him under order 9, rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex parte decree passed on 17.11.97 against him. The petitioner after disposal of the aforesaid Civil Appeal No. 105/99 and Review No. 64/2001 by the Appellate Division started title Execution Case No. 2 of 2001 on 1.3.01 in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka which was re numbered as Execution Case No. 2/2002 on transfer. The opposite party no. 1 obtained an order dated 20.3.02 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 85/97 staying the proceeding of aforesaid Execution Case. The petitioner challenged the said order before the High Court Division in C.R. Case No. 1825/2002 and obtained a rule along with an order of stay of the said order. The rule was made absolute on 22.5.02 and the said impugned order dated 20.3.02 staying the proceeding of Execution 'Case was set aside Opposite party no. 1 Md. Mostaque Hossain filed Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 326/02 in the Appellate Division and obtained an order of stay against the judgment and order dated 22.5.02 passed by the High Court Division and thereafter filed a regular petition for Leave to Appeal bearing no 1064/02 and the same was dismissed on 1.12.02. In the meantime the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by its impugned judgment and order passed on 28.11.02 allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case no. 6/02 and restored the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 setting aside the judgment and decree passed ex parte on 17.11.97 against the opposite party no. 1. Hence this rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner Md. Shahajahan Miah. 

 6. The facts of Civil Revision No. 974/03 are similar to the facts of C.R. No. 305 of 2003 as stated above. The petitioner stated that he and defendant opposite party No. 2 took lease of the suit shop from opposite party No. 1 on the basis of lease agreement dated 19.3.81 paying a salami of Tk. 3,00,000/- and the two shop rooms were converted and amalgamated into one room and a new lease deed was executed on 13.4.88 between the parties. The petitioner and the opposite party No. 2 had been carrying on business in the said shop. The opposite party No. 1 filed S.S.C. suit No. 3/97 against them for their eviction and got decree dated 17.11.97 on contest against opposite party no. 2 and ex parte against the petitioner. The opposite party No. 2 Md. Abdul Hye fought unsuccessfully against the said decree upto appellate Division. The petitioner was also a party in the aforesaid proceedings. Thereafter on the application of the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 under section 151 of the code filed on 18.2.03 the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka vide its impugned order dated 4.3.03 directed to proceed with the execution of decree in title Execution case No. 2/02. Hence this Rules. 

 7. Perused the applications, the impugned judgments and orders and heard the learned Advocates of both the sides. From the facts of both the rules it appears that the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 974/03 as plaintiff instituted S.C.C. Suit No. 3/93 re numbered as S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 for ejectment being deaulter against the opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain and opposite party no.  2 Md. Abdul Hye in Civil Revision No. 305/03 who are petitioner and opposite party no. 2 respectively in Civil Revision No. 974/03. Admittedly they are full brothers and joint tenants in respect of the suit premises. Originally they took lease on rent of two rooms vide agreement dated 19.3.81 from the plaintiff and thereafter on converting and amalgamation of said two rooms into one room they continued in possession there of vide agreement of lease dated 13.4.88 till the S.C.C. suit was filed against them for their ejectment. This is also admitted that the two brothers used to run the business in the same shop and one of the brothers Md. Abdul Hye, who is opposite party no. 2 in both the rules, contested the suit by filing written statements and the suit was decreed on contest against him and ex parte against other brother Md. Mustaque Hossain who is opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/03. The said decree was upheld up to the Appellate Division on contest. Md. Mustaque Hossain in C.R. 974/03 who was defendant no. 2 in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/93 filed an application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the ex parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 85/1997 re numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 6/02 for setting aside the ex parte decree which was allowed by the trial court vide impugned order dated 28.11.02 against which Civil Revision No. 305/03 arose. 

 13 In any case in which a decree is passed ex parte against a defendant he may apply to the court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside, and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the court shall make and order setting aside the decree as against him upon such terms as to costs, payment into court or otherwise as it thinks fit, and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit. 

 9. Referring the above provision Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 305/03 submitted that the order of the trial court dated 4.9.93 passed in the suit shows that the summons have been satisfactorily served upon the (both) defendants. He also submitted that the opposite party no. 1 has not also been able to show that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The opposite party No. 1 having thus failed to satisfy the court that the summons was not duly served upon him nor he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the impugned order is liable to be set aside, Mr. Karim added. He further submitted that the impugned order is neither an objective order nor a speaking order and does not base on evidence. He continued that the trial court neither gave any finding nor an reason whatsoever for setting aside the ex parte decree and as such the impugned order is also liable to be set aside. He also submitted referring the protracted proceedings up to the Appellate Division that the decree passed in S.C.C. Suit against the contesting brother, namely, Md. Abdul Hye having been upheld. The ex parte decree passed against the other brother Md. Mustaque Hossain, the opposite party no. 1 has been merged with the same inasmuch as the decree is indivisible as both the brothers are joint tenants, jointly possess the rented shop and run their business there. Mr. Karim lastly contended that the trial court failed to exercise its jurisdiction while allowing the case in not finding that the miscellaneous case was not maintainable as any security as required under section 17(1) of the Small Cause Courts Act was given by the opposite party No. 1. 

 10. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 contended that the executing court has rightly passed the impugned order directing to proceed with the execution case pursuant to the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division and as such the rule is liable to be discharged with costs. Mr. Karim also submits that the defendant in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 being the opposite parties in Civil Revision No. 305/03 are two full brothers who took lease of the shop jointly as co tenant an have been running the business in the same shop together. The decree dated 17.11.97 passed in S.C.C. suit No. 3/97 is indivisible and binding on both the defendants. Mr. Karim has referred the cases of Mono Mohan Kundu Vs. Nripendra Nath Nandi and others reported in AIR 1937 (Cal) 548 and also the case of Abdul Jalil Bhuiyan and ors. Vs. Majibar Nessa and others reported in 12 DLR (1960) 581. 

 11. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties in Civil Revision No. 305/03 as well as for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/03 found difficult to controvert the submissions of Mr. Karim in the facts and circumstances of the case. He also admitted the joint tenancy, joint possession and running their business in the same suit shop Mr. Ali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 however controverted the submissions made by the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner contending that the learned Assistant Judge has rightly and properly passed the impugned order allowing the miscellaneous case and restoring the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 setting aside the ex parte decree dated 17.11.97. He further submits that as the Opposite Party No. 1 did not contest the suit and the decree having been passed ex parte against him he had rightly initiated the miscellaneous case filing an application under order 9, rule 13 of the Code for restoring the suit to its original file and number on setting aside the exparte decree and such right has not been taken away in the proceedings fought by opposite party no. 2 up to the Appellate Division. He also submits that the exparte decree dated 17.11.97 has not been merged with the decree upheld by the Appellate Division passed on contest against opposite party no. 2 Appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 he submits that the executing court has illegally passed the impugned order dated 4.3.03 directing to proceed with the execution case without considering that the decree dated 17.11.97 passed ex parte against the petitioner in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 has already been set aside and the suit has been restored. Mr. Ali lastly submits that success of the instant rule C.R.974/903 depends upon the fate of Civil Revision No. 305/2003. In support of his submissions Mr. Ali has referred some decisions in cases between Atul Chandra Das Vs. Bhagabati Das and others reported to 18 DLR 1966 81, Makhan Lal Dutta Vs. Joytun Bibi and others reported in 16 DLR 1964 130 Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Barik and another, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 and also reported in 4 BLD (AD) 83. 

 12. In consideration of the fact and circumstances of the case and on perusal of the impugned order dated 28.11.02 allowing the Miscellaneous case, I find substance in the submission of Mr. Karim that in setting aside an ex parte decree under order 9 rule 13 of the Code, the court must be satisfied that there was no due Service of summons or the petitioner was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the case was called on for hearing. But the learned Assistant Judge in passing the Impugned order dated 28.11.02 gave no finding whatsoever nor any reason justifying setting aside the ex parte decree fulfilling the provisions of rule 13 of order 9 of the C.P.C. as quoted above. On the other hand, order vide order No. 10 dated 4.9.93 passed in S.C.C. suit No. 3/93 shows that the summons were duly served upon the defendants satisfactorily. There is also no finding in the impugned order that the defendant opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing in court when the suit was called on for hearing. In that view of the matter as none of the essential conditions of rule 13 of order 9 of the Code having been met the trial court committed an error in passing the impugned order setting aside the ex parte decree allowing his application filed under order 9 rule 13 of the said Code and restoring the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the same is liable to be set aside. It is true that an application under order 9, rule 13 of the Code is subgenera’s and is independent and concurrent remedies are available to an aggrieved party having no nexus with an appeal filed against the contested decree or with a review application under order 47 of the Code, but it is equally true that the fate of the application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code is dependent on the compliance and fulfillment of its requirement. But in the instant case there is absolutely no such compliance and hence the decisions referred by Mr. Ali as mentioned above in support of his contention are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. More-over, admittedly the suit shop is a single room shop taken lease jointly by both the brothers being defendant nos. 1 and 2 in the suit and had admittedly been possessing by them by running their business in the same shop which conclusively indicates that the decree dated 17.11.97 is indivisible. The decisions in the cases reported in A.I.R. 1937 (Cal) 548 and reported in 12 DLR 581 referred by Mr. Karim supports the same. Nowhere at any stage of the proceeding either before this court or Appellate Division there has been any material on record to show that Md. Mustaque Hossain had any clash of interest with his co tenant brother Md. Abdul Hye. In consideration of the facts, circumstances and materials on record of the case as stated above I am of the opinion that the decree passed in S.C.C. suit no. 3/97 is indivisible and the ex parte decree has been merged with the contested decree upheld by the Appellate Division and the same cannot be set aside on an application under order 9 rule 13 of the code and as such the impugned order dated 28.11.02 challenged in C.R. No. 305/02 is liable to be set aside. The decisions in the case between Mono Mohan Kundu Vs. Nripendra Nath Nandi and others, reported in AIR 1937 (Cal) 548 referred by Mr. Karim which has been elaborately quoted and discussed in the case of Abdul Jalil Bhuiyan and ors. Vs. Majibar Nessa Bibi and others, reported in 12 DLR 581 so I refrain from stating the same here to avoid repetition.
